data.one_liner: Parse strings in any format or language into DateTime objects, respecting ISO and RFC standards.
data.what_it_does: Parses date and time strings across various international formats and languages into standard DateTime objects. It supports locale-specific parsing, ISO and major RFC standards, and UNIX timestamps in seconds, milliseconds, microseconds, or nanoseconds.
use_when: You need to parse user-inputted dates that may come in unpredictable or mixed formats.
You need locale-aware date parsing for multiple languages.
You are handling dates adhering to major RFC or ISO standards alongside casual strings.
avoid_when: You only ever deal with strict, uniform ISO 8601 date strings that Dart's built-in DateTime.parse can handle.
strengths: Flexible parsing inspired by Python's dateutil library
Extensive locale support via the intl package
Handles ambiguous date cases via configuration rules
weaknesses: Requires the intl dependency for multi-language support
May require configuration rules to resolve ambiguous date formats like dd/mm/yy vs mm/dd/yy
data.minimal_example:
const parser = AnyDate();
final date = parser.parse('13 Aug 2023');
